commit_message:
[Merged] [heap] Grow new space lazily to target capacity

So far SemiSpaceNewSpace was always eagerly allocating pages to reach
its target capacity (for both semi spaces). This CL relaxes this
and allocates pages lazily when they are needed for allocation.

This improves bomb-workers by about 0.8%.

pr_description:
Allocate new-space pages lazily as allocation requires them. If allocation fails before the active semispace reaches its target capacity, return failure immediately; only consider beyond-capacity expansion once that target has been reached.

Validation: git diff --check passed, and the PR state applies cleanly against the parent revision.

fix_commit_message:
[heap] Add early bailout on allocation slow path for new space

So far it was always the case that we reached
AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity only if the space has already reached
its target capacity. However, now that we lazily allocate new space
pages allocation can also fail when the current capacity is below
the target capacity. E.g. because we run out of virtual memory in
the cage or other OOM situations. This now starts to triggger the
DCHECKs in AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity, which assume that the
space is full. Instead of removing these DCHECKs this CL fixes this
by adding an early bailout in EnsureAllocation(). With this we
only invoke ShouldExpandYoungGenerationOnSlowAllocation() for the
SemiSpaceNewSpace if the space is actually at its capacity.

agent_reasoning: Lazy page allocation removes the assumption that allocation failure means new space has reached its target capacity. Without checking capacity, allocation failures caused by resource exhaustion could enter AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity with its invariants violated. ReachedTargetCapacity compares the active semispace's current capacity against the target, and EnsureAllocation returns false when allocation fails below that target, preserving the beyond-capacity path's preconditions. Changes are limited to the two source files from the supplied correction; no tests were modified.
